title: The projective-line trace and the diagonal integrals
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an integer $n\geq1$, put $A=\Lambda_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. Here Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Put $q:P=\mathbf P^1_S=\mathbf P(\{0,1\};S)\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Coefficients on each small site are the constant sheaf with value the finite discrete ring $A$. Use ordinary module derived categories and derived direct images on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors], not completed coefficient categories. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\nu_T^*$ for the exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. On the etale site put $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1)=\mu_{\ell^n,T}$, with $\mu_{\ell^n,T}(U)=\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^{\ell^n}=1\}$ and scalar action by powers, and $A_{T,\mathrm{et}}(-1)=\mathcal Hom_A(A_{T,\mathrm{et}}(1),A_T)$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-sheaf, lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Set $A_T(\pm1)=\nu_T^*A_{T,\mathrm{et}}(\pm1)$. For any complex $K$ on the pro-etale site, write $K(1)=K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T(1)$ using derived tensor [def-weil-derived-tensor]. Let $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))\in H^2(P_{\mathrm{proet}},A_P(1))$ be the pullback of the etale Kummer boundary of $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [lem-amb-kummer-any-base, def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Then:

1. The map given by the unit and $h$,
$$d_q=(1,h):A_S\oplus A_S(-1)[-2]\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*A_P,$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, compatible with every base change $g:S'\to S$, including non-Noetherian $S'$. Put $P'=\mathbf P^1_{S'}$ and $q':P'\to S'$. Compatibility means that the canonical exchange $\beta_g:g^*Rq_*A_P\to Rq'_*A_{P'}$ carries $g^*d_q$ to the same unit-and-Chern-class map $d_{q'}$ on $S'$.
2. Write $b_q:A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*(A_P(1)[2])$ for the twisted decomposition, whose second component is the adjoint form of $h$. The trace is $\operatorname{Tr}_q=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_q^{-1}$. It is compatible with every base change as above and sends the Kummer class of $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^1_{\bar s}}(1)$, equivalently the class of every rational point of $\mathbf P^1_{\bar s}$, to $1$ on every geometric fibre. The traces on base changes are defined by their corresponding decompositions. The target $Rq_*(A_P(1)[2])$ is the usual notation $Rq_*A_P(1)[2]$ of the blueprint.
3. Put $W=P\times_SP$ [def-pc-fibre-product], let $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ be the projections, and let $\Delta:P\hookrightarrow W$ be the diagonal effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Let $c_\Delta:\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$ be precisely its cycle class of [sk-lem-geo-cartier], the class used in (G6) of the projective-line adjunction unit. Write $\delta:R\Delta_*A_P\to A_W(1)[2]$ for $c_\Delta$ under the canonical identification $R\Delta_*A_P\cong\Delta_*A_P$ from closed direct-image exactness [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. For $a=1,2$, let $\alpha_a:A_P\xrightarrow{\sim}R(p_a)_*R\Delta_*A_P$ be the canonical derived-composition identification from $p_a\Delta=\operatorname{id}_P$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Then
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{p_a}\circ R(p_a)_*(\delta)\circ\alpha_a=\operatorname{id}_{A_P}\qquad(a=1,2).$$
Thus the displayed integrals include the canonical identification of their source with $A_P$.

In particular, (1)--(2) hold over every scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible: take the Noetherian base $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/\ell]$ and apply the asserted arbitrary-base-change compatibility to its structure morphism $T\to S_0$. This gives exactly the unit, Kummer decomposition and trace over $T$.

proof.text: The projective-space pullback formula identifies each $p_a$ with a projective line over $P$, and identifies the projective line after any $g:S'\to S$. The projective-space properness theorem makes $q,q'$ and $p_a$ proper. A proper morphism is separated and of finite type; finite type includes quasi-compactness, and a separated morphism is quasi-separated. Thus all these morphisms are qcqs, without a Noetherian condition on $S'$. These facts give the projective-line identifications and proper qcqs hypotheses used below.

source.place: Proof (1) and (3): projective-space identifications, properness and qcqs hypotheses

proof.text: Since $S$ is Noetherian and $q$ is of finite type, $P$ is Noetherian as well. Each $p_a:W\to P$ is of finite type with Noetherian target $P$, so the same finite-type theorem also makes $W$ Noetherian, as required for the projection formula applied to $p_a$. Finally $\Delta$ is a closed immersion by separatedness of $q$, hence proper and qcqs too. These are precisely the hypotheses needed below for the ordinary decomposition over $S$ and $P$ and for bounded-below direct-image comparison for $q,q',p_a,\Delta$. To verify the Cartier hypothesis rather than assume it, work over an affine base $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and the four products of standard charts. On equal-index charts the diagonal has equation $x-y$ in $R[x,y]$; on mixed charts it has equation $xy-1$. The first is monic in $x$, so multiplication is injective. For the second, if $(xy-1)\sum_{k=0}^m a_k(y)x^k=0$, its constant coefficient gives $a_0=0$ and the coefficient of $x^k$ gives $a_k=ya_{k-1}$, whence all $a_k=0$. Thus these equations are non-zero-divisors over every ring and remain so after arbitrary base change. This proves that $\Delta$ is effective Cartier. Its complement is quasi-compact: use a finite affine cover of the Noetherian $S$ and these four charts; in each chart the complement is the principal affine open defined by the corresponding equation. The pro-etale ringed open/closed theorem therefore applies to the constant coefficient sheaf $A_W$ and says $\Delta_*$ on modules is exact. Applying it to an injective resolution gives the canonical identification $R\Delta_*A_P=\Delta_*A_P$, including their restriction units.

source.place: Proof (1) and (3): Noetherian targets and regular equations for the diagonal

proof.text: Work first on the ordinary small etale sites, with $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and $N=\ell^n$. All coefficient hypotheses hold: $N\geq1$, $A$ is finite, $NA=0$, and $N$ is invertible on every scheme over $S$. The current statement of [thm-amb-p1-decomposition] applies to these data in the ordinary etale constant-$A$ module categories. Since $A=\mathbf Z/N$, its scalar extension of the Kummer class is the identity scalar extension, and its twist $\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ is canonically $\mu_N$, exactly our etale twist. Its convention $e_0=t^{-1}e_1$ for $t=x_1/x_0$ agrees with our $\mathcal O(1)$. Its second component $h_{\mathrm{et}}:A_S(-1)[-2]\to Rq_{\mathrm{et},*}A_P$ is defined by the adjoint of $1\otimes c_1(\mathcal O(1))$ followed by evaluation, so it is precisely the unit-and-Chern-class map $d_q^{\mathrm{et}}=(1,h_{\mathrm{et}})$, and the theorem says that this map is an isomorphism. The locally free rank-one twists and their pullback/evaluation identifications are those of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Its twisted version is the explicitly normalized decomposition $b_q^{\mathrm{et}}:A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_{\mathrm{et},*}(A_P(1)[2])$ in the ordinary finite projective-line interface. Its second component is exactly the Kummer class, not an unspecified generator. The definition of the ordinary trace is $t_q^{\mathrm{et}}=\operatorname{pr}_2(b_q^{\mathrm{et}})^{-1}$. The same facts apply over the Noetherian base $P$ to either $p_a$. The proper projection formula with the invertible finite twist identifies this $b_q^{\mathrm{et}}$ with $d_q^{\mathrm{et}}$ twisted by $(1)[2]$: the hyperplane summand becomes $A_S$, and the unit summand becomes $A_S(1)[2]$. Its Noetherian hypotheses hold for $q$ and $p_a$ by steps 1--2.

source.place: Proof (1), projective-line decomposition; Proof (2), definition of the trace

proof.text: Here is also the ordinary-etale compatibility for an arbitrary $g:S'\to S$. Proper base change for the torsion ring $A$ gives isomorphisms $g^{-1}Rq_{\mathrm{et},*}E\xrightarrow{\beta_g^{\mathrm{et}}}Rq'_{\mathrm{et},*}g_P^{-1}E$ for both $E=A_P$ and $E=A_P(1)[2]$, with no Noetherian condition on $S'$. The twist pullback theorem identifies all their twists. The pullback of the unit is the unit by the identity/pasting rules for adjunction mates. For the second component, the infinity divisor on the projective line has local equation $t=0$ on the chart at infinity and is empty on the complementary chart. Its ideal is invertible, and dualizing its transition function gives $\mathcal O(1)$. It remains Cartier after any base change since multiplication by the indeterminate $t$ is injective on $R[t]$ for every ring $R$. The supported Kummer morphism, and its composite with the divisor unit, therefore pull back to those of infinity on $P'$. Its composite is $c_1(\mathcal O(1))$. Consequently $\beta_g^{\mathrm{et}}g^{-1}d_q^{\mathrm{et}}=d_{q'}^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\beta_g^{\mathrm{et}}g^{-1}b_q^{\mathrm{et}}=b_{q'}^{\mathrm{et}}$, with the evident pullback identifications on their sources. This proves that the two maps on $S'$ are isomorphisms too; no decomposition theorem over a non-Noetherian base was invoked.

source.place: Proof (1), last two sentences: base change of the unit and the Kummer class; Stacks Tag 0F0C (lemma-proper-base-change-mod-n)

proof.text:
For every scheme morphism $r:V	o T$ appearing here, $Rr_*$ means the total right derived ordinary direct image of constant-$A$ module sheaves, computed on K-injective resolutions as defined in [sk-def-sfb-finite-derived-functors], with coefficient category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}_A$. We use that node here for this definition of $Rr_*$ and its bounded-below version. The comparison pullback is the termwise exact functor of [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]; its exactness and preservation of the bounded-below range are supplied by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Apply the exact derived comparison pullback $
u_T^*$ to these maps. It preserves their direct sums and shifts; its tensor comparison identifies the pulled-back finite twists with the twists in the statement. For any of $r=q,q',p_a,\Delta$, write $C_r:
u_T^*Rr_{\mathrm{et},*}E\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_{\mathrm{proet},*}
u_V^*E$ for direct-image comparison. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1--2, and the inputs are sheaves, their shifts, or $R\Delta_*A_P$ on the etale site; the last is canonically a sheaf by the closed-immersion exactness stated in [lem-amb-p1-diagonal-integrals], so all inputs are bounded below; an unbounded comparison theorem is unnecessary. Thus $d_q=C_q
u_S^*d_q^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $b_q=C_q
u_S^*b_q^{\mathrm{et}}$ are isomorphisms with the required unit and Chern components.

source.place: Proof (1), transport to the pro-etale site: exact comparison and bounded-below direct-image comparison

proof.text:
More explicitly, comparison commutes with pullback, and the mate-pasting rule gives, after those pullback identifications,
$$\beta_g^{\mathrm{proet}}\,g^*C_q=C_{q'}\,\nu_{S'}^*(\beta_g^{\mathrm{et}}).$$
Indeed each exchange is the mate of the pullback commutation square; pasting that square with the two comparison squares in either order gives the same square. Applying this equality to the two component equations of step 4 proves the claimed compatibility for every $g$ on the pro-etale sites. In particular it proves (1), including arbitrary base change, and identifies the pro-etale twisted decomposition with the one obtained from the etale normalization.

source.place: Proof (1), transport to the pro-etale site: mate-pasting and base-change compatibility

proof.text:
Let $\iota_2:A_S\to A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S$. Since $h=b_q\iota_2$ in adjoint form, $\operatorname{Tr}_qh=\operatorname{pr}_2b_q^{-1}b_q\iota_2=\operatorname{id}_{A_S}$. If $\beta$ denotes the twisted exchange from step 6, its equation $b_{q'}=\beta g^*b_q$ gives
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{q'}\beta=\operatorname{pr}_2 b_{q'}^{-1}\beta=\operatorname{pr}_2g^*(b_q^{-1})=g^*\operatorname{Tr}_q.$$
This is trace compatibility, including pullback to any geometric point, and proves that the trace of the geometric-fibre hyperplane class is $1$. It also shows that $\operatorname{Tr}_q=C_q^{-1}$ followed by $\nu_S^*t_q^{\mathrm{et}}$, a description used in the final step. For the non-Noetherian bases needed by the tower-class citer, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/\ell]$ is Noetherian: localization preserves the ascending-chain condition on ideals (each ideal is the extension of its contraction, so an ascending chain contracts to an ascending chain in $\mathbf Z$). Every scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible has its structure map $T\to S_0$, obtained on affine opens by the unique ring homomorphism $\mathbf Z[1/\ell]\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_T)$. Steps 4--6 and the displayed trace equation applied to this map give (1)--(2) over $T$ with exactly their intrinsic unit and Kummer components. No Noetherian assumption on $T$ is made.

source.place: Proof (2): projection onto the second summand and its compatibility; algebraic consequences of steps 2--4

proof.text: On $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ for a geometric residue field $\Omega$, a rational point $x=[a:b]$ is the zero divisor of the nonzero linear form $bX_0-aX_1$. On $U_0=D_+(X_0)$ with $t=X_1/X_0$ and $U_1=D_+(X_1)$ with $u=X_0/X_1$, its ideal has generators $f_0=b-at$ and $f_1=bu-a$. These are non-zero-divisors: each is either a nonzero constant or a nonzero linear polynomial over the field $\Omega$. On the overlap $f_0=t f_1$, so the dual ideal has bases $e_0=t^{-1}e_1$, exactly the transition of $\mathcal O(1)$. Thus $\mathcal O(x)\cong\mathcal O(1)$. For $a=0$ the two equations are $b$ and $bu$; for $b=0$ they are $-at$ and $-a$, so this calculation includes both coordinate points. By the definition of the Kummer Chern class, equal line-bundle classes have equal boundaries. Hence the rational-point class is $h$, proving the remaining assertion of (2) by step 7.

source.place: Proof (2), last sentence: the class of every rational point is the hyperplane class

proof.text:
First keep the ordinary-etale supported Kummer class as an auxiliary map, denoted $\delta_{\mathrm{et}}$, and put $\widetilde\delta=\nu_W^*(\delta_{\mathrm{et}})C_\Delta^{-1}$. This notation does not identify it with $c_\Delta$. The ordinary-etale diagonal-integrals lemma, at $N=\ell^n$ and $A=\Lambda_n$, states
$$t_{p_a}^{\mathrm{et}}R(p_a)_{\mathrm{et},*}(\delta_{\mathrm{et}})\alpha_a^{\mathrm{et}}=\operatorname{id}_{A_P}\quad(a=1,2).$$
All its hypotheses hold by steps 1--2. Apply $\nu_P^*$. Naturality of direct-image comparison gives
$$R(p_a)_{\mathrm{proet},*}(\widetilde\delta)R(p_a)_{\mathrm{proet},*}(C_\Delta)C_{p_a,R\Delta_*A}=C_{p_a,A_W(1)[2]}\nu_P^*\bigl(R(p_a)_{\mathrm{et},*}\delta_{\mathrm{et}}\bigr).$$
Its composition compatibility and the identity comparison for $p_a\Delta=\operatorname{id}$ identify
$$\alpha_a=R(p_a)_*(C_\Delta)C_{p_a,R\Delta_*A}\nu_P^*\alpha_a^{\mathrm{et}}.$$
By step 7, $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_a}=\nu_P^*t_{p_a}^{\mathrm{et}}C_{p_a,A_W(1)[2]}^{-1}$. Substitution cancels the comparison maps and yields
$$\operatorname{Tr}_{p_a}R(p_a)_*(\widetilde\delta)\alpha_a=\operatorname{id}_{A_P}.$$

source.place: Proof (3): transport the auxiliary ordinary-etale diagonal integral through comparison

proof.text:
We now pass to the class actually fixed by the unit, using only an equality of integrals. Let $u_\Delta:A_W\to R\Delta_*A_P$ be restriction (the derived adjunction unit), and $\eta_{p_a}:A_P\to R(p_a)_*A_W$ the usual inverse-image/direct-image unit. The composite-adjunction formula is
$$\alpha_a=R(p_a)_*(u_\Delta)\eta_{p_a}.$$
Here the formula uses the canonical $\kappa_{p_a,\Delta}$ of the derived-composition node, not an arbitrary isomorphism. To verify its normalization, choose a K-injective resolution $A_P\to I$ and a K-injective resolution $j:\Delta_*I\to J$. The unit for the composite adjunction is $R(p_a)_*(\eta_\Delta)\eta_{p_a}$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Under the resolution models its value on the constant sheaf is represented by the restriction maps
$$A_P\longrightarrow(p_a)_*\Delta_*I\xrightarrow{(p_a)_*j}(p_a)_*J.$$
The first arrow is exactly $A_P\to I$, since $p_a\Delta=\operatorname{id}$ and the two underived restrictions compose to identity restriction. The second arrow represents $\kappa_{p_a,\Delta}$ by the explicit normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Thus this is the canonical $\alpha_a$, proving the displayed formula; equivalently it is unit compatibility under the composite-adjunction mate-pasting rule.

source.place: Proof (3), unit normalization: canonical composite-adjunction unit and pushforward-composition normalization

proof.text:
By [sk-lem-geo-cartier], with $r=n$, $\Lambda=A$ and the Cartier divisor verified in step 2, our $\delta$ satisfies $\delta u_\Delta=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. The supported-Kummer statement gives $\delta_{\mathrm{et}}u_\Delta^{\mathrm{et}}=c_1^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. Comparison preserves the unit, so $C_\Delta\nu_W^*u_\Delta^{\mathrm{et}}=u_\Delta$; hence $\widetilde\delta u_\Delta=\nu_W^*c_1^{\mathrm{et}}(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))=c_1(\mathcal O_W(\Delta))$. These are the same Chern class with the positive sign specified in the two cited statements. Consequently, for each projection,
$$\begin{aligned}
R(p_a)_*(\delta)\alpha_a
&=R(p_a)_*(\delta u_\Delta)\eta_{p_a}\\
&=R(p_a)_*(\widetilde\delta u_\Delta)\eta_{p_a}
=R(p_a)_*(\widetilde\delta)\alpha_a.
\end{aligned}$$
Compose with $\operatorname{Tr}_{p_a}$ and use the auxiliary integral already proved to obtain (3) for precisely $c_\Delta$. The argument does not infer equality of the two supported morphisms from equality of their composites with the unit, and uses no conservativity assertion for arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Proof (3): compare the two Chern-class composites and conclude the integral for c_Delta

Step 1 separates projective qcqs hypotheses from the diagonal Cartier calculation; step 4 separates exact comparison from mate-pasting base-change compatibility; step 7 separates auxiliary etale transport, canonical composite-adjunction normalization, and comparison of the two Chern-class constructions. The statement and route are unchanged, and no new nodes were needed because every extracted argument is supplied by existing cited nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1--6 realize proof (1), including the qcqs and Noetherian hypotheses, Cartier chart calculation, ordinary-etale decomposition, arbitrary base change and exact comparison transport. Steps 7--8 realize proof (2), trace normalization, extension to arbitrary bases and rational-point classes. Steps 9--11 realize proof (3): auxiliary etale integral, canonical composite-adjunction normalization, and comparison of the two Chern-class composites for the exact Cartier class fixed by (G5)--(G6).
